title: Georgia Statewide Ballot Measures
description: Curated statewide ballot measures (constitutional amendments and statewide referenda) for Georgia. One file spans multiple election cycles; consumers select measures by electionDate. Measures are never deleted after an election -- they are retained as a historical record and their outcome is captured via the terminal `passed`/`failed` status and the `results` object. A measure that never reached the ballot ends at `not-on-ballot` instead.

generatedAt.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) or ISO timestamp the file was last curated.

election.description: Human-readable name of the focal election, e.g. 'November 3, 2026 General Election'. When the file spans multiple elections this describes the current/upcoming one.

electionDate.description: Default election date (YYYY-MM-DD) applied to any measure that omits its own electionDate.

schemaVersion.description: Version of this schema the file targets.

certifiedCount.description: Optional convenience count of certified measures for the focal election.

potentialCount.description: Optional convenience count of potential measures for the focal election.

status.description: Lifecycle stage. 'potential' = passed the General Assembly but not yet certified for the ballot. 'certified' = certified by the Secretary of State and on the ballot. 'not-on-ballot' = terminal: tracked as potential but never referred to voters (e.g. one chamber never agreed to the other's substitute before adjournment). Retained as a historical record and MUST NOT be presented as something a voter can still vote on. 'passed'/'failed' = terminal outcome recorded after the election is certified; these serve as the authoritative pass/fail tag and drive the 'Ballot measure passed/failed' label in the UI.

title.description: Full descriptive title of the measure.

summary.description: Plain-language summary of what the measure does.

statusNote.description: Optional note about the measure's current lifecycle position (e.g. what still has to happen for a 'potential' measure to reach the ballot, or why a 'not-on-ballot' measure never reached voters).

electionDate.description: Election date (YYYY-MM-DD) this measure appears on. Falls back to metadata.electionDate when absent. Consumers use this to select the focal election and to archive past-cycle measures from active display without deleting them.

identifier.description: Bill/resolution number that referred the measure to the ballot.

url.description: Link to the enabling legislation on legis.ga.gov.

enablingLegislation.description: The General Assembly bill/resolution that placed the measure on the ballot.

intent.description: Why this measure was put to voters, in plain language, drawn from official material (the ballot question, the enabling legislation, the sponsors' stated purpose). Descriptive, never persuasive: it says what the measure is FOR, not whether to vote for it. Anything contested belongs in `sources` as an attributed link instead.

sources.description: A labelled reading list for this measure, so a voter can read the arguments at their origin. VoteGA does not characterise or summarise the positions -- each entry points at a document and says what KIND of document it is. An entry is never VoteGA's own view. Where no organised support or opposition exists, the honest result is no entry of that kind: do NOT add a weak or manufactured one for symmetry.

label.description: Neutral description of the document, e.g. 'Position on HR 1243'. Must not paraphrase the argument.

publisher.description: Who published it, named as the voter would recognise them.

kind.description: 'official' = government or legislative material. 'news' = reporting. 'support'/'oppose' = a party to the debate, labelled so a reader can weigh it. 'analysis' = research or advocacy organisation not formally campaigning.

published.description: Publication date (YYYY-MM-DD) where known. An argument from before a campaign formed is not the argument now, so the date is shown to the reader.

note.description: Optional factual caveat, e.g. that a link is paywalled.

opposition.description: What was found when looking for organised opposition, stated plainly -- including 'none identified', which is information a voter should have rather than an empty section. Never a characterisation of opponents' motives.

explainer.description: Link to VoteGA's own plain-language explanation of this measure -- what it does and what a yes or no vote means. Usually a section of a per-cycle explainer post, so the URL carries the fragment and is stored per measure rather than derived: a later cycle's measure must not inherit an earlier cycle's post. Keep `anchorCheck` in scripts/validate_ballot_measures.py passing when a heading is reworded.

label.description: Optional link text override; the UI supplies a default.

fullText.description: URL to the full amendment/referendum text, or null if unavailable.

noPercent.description: Percent voting no. If omitted, consumers derive it as 100 - yesPercent.

passed.description: Whether the measure was approved by voters. Should agree with the terminal `status` (passed/failed).

totalVotes.description: Total votes cast on the measure, if reported.

results.description: Certified vote outcome. Null until results are certified after the election.

allOf.$comment: A terminal status must carry a results object, and a results object implies a terminal status -- the two must not disagree.
